# SpriteFont

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Fonts` · class

```csharp
public sealed class SpriteFont : IContent
```

Types: [`IContent`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/IContent.md)

A font drawn with [`SpriteBatch`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/SpriteBatch.md) from glyphs packed into one or more atlas pages, built from a TTF/OTF font (and optional fallback fonts) by the toolkit SpriteFontContent pipeline.

## Remarks

All metrics are in pixels at [`EmSize`](#emsize), the size the glyphs were rendered at. Draw at another size by scaling: `scale = new Vector2(pixelSize / font.EmSize)`. Distance-field fonts (`GlyphFormat.Sdf`, `GlyphFormat.Msdf`, `GlyphFormat.Mtsdf`) stay sharp at any scale, and `GlyphFormat.Bitmap` fonts are pixel-exact at scale 1. Text draws with the font's [`Shader`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Shader.md), in any batch, so there's nothing to set up to draw it.

Text is laid out from the top-left corner of the first line: the baseline of each line is [`Ascender`](#ascender) below its top, and lines are [`LineHeight`](#lineheight) apart.

There is no text shaping: each code point draws its own glyph, left to right. No ligatures, bidirectional reordering or contextual forms are applied, so Arabic, Hebrew and Indic scripts don't draw correctly, and an emoji sequence draws as its separate code points.

Gets the height of the font's ascender above the baseline, which is the distance from the top of a line to its baseline.

### CapHeight

```csharp

```

Gets the height of the font's capital letters above the baseline, from the font's OS/2 table or its "H", or zero if the font doesn't give it.

Gets the size, in pixels per em, that the glyphs were rendered at. Every other metric of the font is in pixels at this size.

### Shader

```csharp
public Shader Shader { get; set; }
```

Types: [`Shader`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Shader.md)

Gets or sets the shader this font's text draws with, whichever the sprite batch is using, which it goes back to after the text. It starts as the toolkit's text shader, one shared by every font, which draws every glyph format and every [`TextEffects`](TextEffects.md).

The text shader has no parameters: each font's and effect's settings travel with each glyph, so text in many fonts and effects draws together, split only where the atlas page changes. A custom shader can read the same settings, as `TEXCOORD1`; the toolkit's `spritefont.slang` describes them. It stays yours to release.

## Methods

### MeasureString

```csharp
public Vector2 MeasureString(int codePoint, float tracking = 0)
```

Measures the advance width and line height of a single code point.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `tracking` | The additional spacing applied after each character, in unscaled font units. Zero uses the spacing defined by the font; positive values loosen it and negative values tighten it. This is uniform spacing, unlike the pair-specific adjustment of kerning. |
| `codePoint` | The character. |

```csharp

```

|---|---|
